title: Nelson's first bands: Garber, Kit Harris and Sidney Desvigne
summary: Nelson moves to New Orleans, plays with Kit Harris and then Sidney Desvigne, working clubs and country clubs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Cabarets, honky-tonks and the Storyville nightlife scene

blocks.x: What was your first band you played with?

Joseph Garber was out in the country, out in the Polandville. Then I came to New Orleans. My first wife, she died. And that's when I met Kit Harris. Kit Harris, yes. And I played with him. And one night I was at the Bulls. And I met Sidney Desvene and I started playing with him.
What kind of band did Kit Harris have?
Oh, he had a little Dixieland. About six, seven pieces.
Was it different from the Joe Garber.
Oh, yes, it was. Joe Garber didn't have a Dixieland. He played mostly stocks and arrangements.
Play that. And then Joe Harris got you started on something else, huh?

Kit Harris. I mean, you got you started on something else. Yes, yes. I came and started playing with him, yes. Then after I went to Sidney Desvene, and I was quite a young man. I was in my 20s, late 20s, rather. And I started playing with him. We used to play at the Bulls for the culling on Tuesdays, and play at the Pethean Temple, or the Roof Garden for the culling on Mondays. And all the rest of the week, we was playing for the White. All the leading clubs out in the city of New Orleans, like the Southern Yacht, Jewish Country Club, New Orleans Country Club, Colonial Country Club, all the leading hotels in the city of New Orleans. We'd go in every night.
